endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Define a "default-off" posture for newly released AI features on enterprise platforms wherever the platform permits, pending governance review.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether keeping new AI features switched off by default until governance review reduces harm, and no study documents how often unreviewed features activate through vendor releases. The recommendation rests on a single framework endorsement from CHAI, which frames default-off as a posture to adopt wherever the platform permits.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The support comes from one framework source using "should" language, which reflects expert judgment rather than measured outcomes.

The CHAI playbook language limits the practice to cases where the platform permits a default-off setting. This wording suggests that some enterprise platforms may not offer that control, so the recommendation may depend on contract terms with vendors as much as on internal governance policy. No supplied source reports how many platforms allow it.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that measure how often vendor releases activate AI features before governance review, and that compare systems with and without a default-off policy on review completion rates, time to feature availability, clinician workarounds, and patient-level adverse events.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of this practice exists, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether a default-off policy protects or delays benefits for these groups remains unknown, and safety-net systems with smaller governance teams may face longer review queues that no study has examined.
